summary: NHTSA acknowledged awareness of the AMC six-cylinder engine situation and stated it did not use any CID reduction for AMC in establishing the NPRM scenario, relying only on N/V reduction; the final EIS was revised to account for the separate class of recreational-type NPA's including AMC's Jeep CJ's.
text:
Analysis. NHTSA did not "double count" in arriving at the AFES. The (CID) x (N/V) reduction indicated by GM in their June 1976 submission to NHTSA was only considered This matter is explained further in the preamble to the final rule. The analysis does not include a 12.2 percent reduction in (CID)x(N/V) in addition to a 13.3 percent reduction. The equation used to project fuel economy changes resulting from CID changes is different from the relationship used to project weight reductions resulting from CID reductions. Both equations produce acceptable results in general but do not agree with practice for some specific cases. NHTSA was aware of the situation for the AMC six cylinder engines where their fuel economy is comparable and therefore did not use any CID reduction in the NPRM for AMC in establishing a scenario by which they could meet the standard. It was assumed that only N/V reduction would be used. However, in projecting possible impacts on natural resources, the possibility of CID reductions, which would reflect substitutions of 6 cylinder engines for V-8 engines, was investigated. The draft EIS therefore included weight reduction resulting

from CID reduction for AMC. This has been revised for the final EIS due to the separate class of recreational-type NPA's with off-road capabilites which would include AMC's Jeep CJ's.
